keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. "Geographical range: Korean Peninsula"; no area or frontier on the page; one shape holds because the page dates no change of extent (only an inland movement of settlement in the Late Jeulmun).

ledger.note: 6000 BCE: the Early Jeulmun shell-midden fishers and foragers hold the Korean Peninsula ("The Early Jeulmun period (c. 6000-3500 BC)"; the lead dates the culture from 8000 BC).
3500 BCE: the Middle Jeulmun begins: "Middle Jeulmun period (c. 3500-2000 BC)"; millet cultivation appears at Dongsam-dong.
2000 BCE: the Late Jeulmun begins: "Late Jeulmun period (c. 2000-1500 BC)", with "the movement of people into the interior".

1500 BCE: the Jeulmun gives way to the Mumun pottery period ("Followed by: Mumun pottery period", "c. 1500-300 BC"); "Slash-and-burn cultivators who used Mumun pottery displaced people using Jeulmun period subsistence patterns".

certainty.note: No border is recorded; the coast is the edge.

notes: Jeulmun (Chulmun) pottery period of the Korean Peninsula; the infobox gives 'c. 8000 - c. 1500 BC' and the lead 'broadly spanning the period of 8000-1500 BC'. The lead calls 8000-3500 'Incipient to Early' and 3500-1500 'Middle and Late'; the body gives 'Early Jeulmun period (c. 6000-3500 BC)', 'Middle Jeulmun period (c. 3500-2000 BC)' and 'Late Jeulmun period (c. 2000-1500 BC)': the lead and body disagree on the early phase's start; the body's 6000 and 3500 are used. The dossier starts at -6000 and runs beyond the 3400 BCE horizon on purpose: Cliopatria draws nothing on the peninsula before Gojoseon (197 BCE). Extent: 'Korean Peninsula' (infobox); shell-midden sites at 'Ulsan Sejuk-ri, Dongsam-dong, and Ga-do Island'; Yunggimun pottery 'at southern sites such as Gosan-ni in Jeju Province'; Jitam-ri in North Korea; 'at least 14 Middle Jeulmun period sites have yielded evidence of cultivation'; the Late Jeulmun saw 'the movement of people into the interior' (settlement shift, not drawn). The whole peninsula is drawn (confidence 2: sites are coastal and scattered, and the page gives no inland frontier). End: 'The Mumun period is preceded by the Jeulmun pottery period (c. 8000-1500 BC)'; 'Slash-and-burn cultivators who used Mumun pottery displaced people using Jeulmun period subsistence patterns'. The Mumun pottery period (c. 1500-300 BC) has no dossier (counterpart). No area figure.
